text:
maria: Quick question — can we standardize attaching an incident ID + minimal trace payload when an automatic fallback fires? Right now rollouts just log a generic event and it's hard to connect to incidents or SLO regressions.

ashwin: +1. We get asked for this on support calls. If a fallback triggers we should include: incident_id, route, decision_reason, model_variant, and a short failure stack (first 3 lines).

julia: Agree. Two UX things: 1) the console should surface the most recent fallback incidents under the rollout detail panel; 2) an option to opt-out for sensitive deployments (PII concerns).

samir: For opt-out we can add a boolean `include_audit_trace` on the rollout policy. Default true for Dedicated/Hosted, default false for Private unless customer opts in.

maria: That sounds reasonable. For Hosted maybe we keep an allowlist so ops can request full traces for debug, otherwise we send a redacted summary.

kevin: Implementation note — telemetry pipeline currently accepts an event: `fallback_activated` with `meta` blob. We need a stricter schema so we can index by incident_id and run queries by rollout_id fast.

ashwin: Schema suggestion (minimal):
```json
{
  "rollout_id": "string",
  "fallback_policy_id": "string",
  "incident_id": "string|null",
  "decision_reason": "string",
  "model_variant": "string",
  "latency_ms": "int",
  "error_code": "string|null",
  "trace_snippet": "string|null"  // first 3 lines
}
```

julia: We should also record whether the fallback was automatic vs manual toggle. That's essential for postmortems.

maria: Good catch. Add `trigger_type: automatic|manual|scheduled`.

ops-bot: NOTICE: When enabled, fallback events will be routed to `#incidents` if incident_id is present and severity >= P2.

samir: UX question — do we show these audit events in the rollout timeline as expandable items? Or keep them in a separate "fallback incidents" tab?

kevin: Timeline gets noisy quickly for high-traffic rollouts. I vote for a dedicated tab with a condensed timeline + quick filters (by incident_id, model_variant, decision_reason). Clicking an event expands the trace snippet and links to the incident on the incidents board.

maria: Also need retention policy: telemetry team suggests 90 days for full trace_snippet, 365 days for metadata. Any objections?

ashwin: 90/365 seems ok. Maybe configurable per-org for enterprise customers.

julia: Two more items: 1) Console should let SREs replay the event in a simulator view (redact secrets) so they can reproduce the decision without hitting prod; 2) Add a lightweight regression flag so evals can pick up when fallback rate changes > X% over baseline.

samir: For the simulator we can return a sanitized request/response snapshot and the policy decision path. That shouldn't be hard.

maria: Ops integration — if fallback has `incident_id` attach that ID to the rollout's audit log entry and link it in the runbook export. That'll make postmortems a lot faster.

kevin: I'll sketch a PR for the telemetry schema + index plan. If we agree on fields I'll add the ingestion validation and a migration to normalize old events.

maria: Great — next steps: kevin to PR schema, samir to prototype console tab mock, julia to add opt-out wording for Private deployments, ashwin to confirm retention defaults with telemetry. I'll follow up in a short doc. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-schema-validator (branch: fallback-audit-schema)

maria: thanks — keeping this lightweight. If anyone wants to sync 1:1, ping me.
